documents.title: Hybrid BiLSTM-Graph Neural Networks Learn Efficient Secondary Structure Representations for Protein-Protein Interface Prediction.
documents.abstract: Protein-protein interfaces (PPIs) are essential for numerous biological processes and represent attractive targets for drug discovery and protein engineering. Although recent protein language models have enabled powerful sequence representations for downstream structural prediction tasks, they require substantial computational resources and produce general-purpose embeddings that are not optimized for specific applications. In this work, we investigate whether task-specific representation learning can provide a computationally efficient alternative for PPI prediction. Proteins are represented

documents.title: Ecological Context in Computational Discovery of Microbiome-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides.
documents.abstract: Computational mining of microbiomes has expanded antimicrobial peptide (AMP) discovery from individual organisms to millions of predicted sequences. The challenge is now to identify candidates that merit experimental investigation and to determine what their validation reveals about biological function. Ecological information may describe sequence provenance, support interpretation after prediction, guide candidate prioritization or contribute directly to model development. These uses are distinct, and the presence of ecological metadata does not by itself show that context improved discovery.

documents.title: Predicting Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares Using Wearable Device Data: Deep Learning Study.
documents.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares are common and unpredictable. Current monitoring relies on episodic clinical visits and laboratory testing, thereby limiting the ability to anticipate disease worsening. Wearable devices may support continuous remote monitoring, but models must account for missing real-world data, heterogeneous consumer devices, and the distinction between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation.

documents.title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein-protein ΔΔG prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation,

documents.title: Protein sequence domain annotation using a language model.
documents.abstract: Protein domain annotation underlies large-scale functional inference and is commonly performed by scanning sequences against libraries of profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). We describe PSALM, a protein domain annotation method that combines (i) a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with (ii) a per-residue domain-state classifier and (iii) a structured probabilistic decoder that produces a single, non-overlapping set of domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. On a benchmark of 76.9M protein sequences with 107M annotated domains, PSALM attains a domain-detection sensiti

documents.title: MissenseDB: proteome-wide human missense variant effect prediction database with structural context.
documents.abstract: Missense variant-effect predictors now provide proteome-scale estimates of amino acid substitution impact, but their outputs remain distributed across independent resources and are difficult to explore jointly with protein structural and human-variation context. We present MissenseDB, a residue-centric database integrating three architecturally distinct transformer-based predictors, AlphaMissense, VESM-3B, and VESPA, across the reviewed human proteome. MissenseDB contains 10 734 339 residue positions across 19 436 canonical human proteins, with complete three-predictor coverage for 19 434 prot

documents.title: ARCADE: Controllable Codon Design from Foundation Models via Activation Engineering.
documents.abstract: Coding sequence design requires optimizing multiple biological properties, which may be either aligned or in trade-off, and are typically measured as continuous-valued metrics. However, existing codon design methods lack explicit control over these objectives. Moreover, current controllable generation techniques are largely developed for discrete, human-interpretable attributes, leaving a gap in controllably steering continuous biological properties in genomic sequence design.

documents.title: LiteMicroFormer: A Lightweight Attention-Guided Transformer with Adaptive Cluster Under-Sampling for Metagenomic Disease Prediction.
documents.abstract: High-dimensional microbial abundance profiles, limited sample sizes, and severe class imbalance make accurate disease prediction from human gut metagenomics challenging. To address these limitations, we propose LiteMicroFormer, a lightweight attention-guided transformer framework for disease-specific binary classification using species-level microbiome profiles and metadata. LiteMicroFormer embeds species values, applies feature-gating attention, extracts microbial representations through a transformer, fuses metadata, and uses attention pooling to capture informative low-complexity patterns.

documents.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine dental imaging captures cumulative dentoalveolar and periodontal changes, offering a non-invasive window into both chronological aging and physiological senescence. While task-specific deep learning models have been widely explored in dental radiology, the zero-shot diagnostic performance of commercial Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in adult populations remains underinvestigated. The aim of this study was to benchmark the zero-shot diagnostic accuracy and repeatability of a commercial MLLM against human clinicians of varying experience levels in estimat

documents.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
documents.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.

documents.title: Enhanced prognosis stratification following surgery for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to optimize clinical decisions by reflecting tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
documents.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.

documents.title: Machine learning and the protein corona: importance of nanoparticle, protein, and experimental features.
documents.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) present in any biological environment are rapidly coated with a "corona" of proteins on the surface of the NPs. This protein corona, rather than the bare NP, determines the biological response to the protein-NP complex. The use of machine learning to predict which proteins will adsorb on the surface of a NP would accelerate the development of new NPs. We provide a detailed examination of two random forest models, random forest regression (RFR) and classification (RFC), to determine how corona prediction is impacted by the biophysics, data structure, and statistics of the sy

documents.title: Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Highlight IAPP as a Molecular Feature Associated with β-Cell Identity Remodeling in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
documents.abstract: β-cell identity remodeling is an important feature of β-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but its associated molecular characteristics remain incompletely understood. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene set variation analysis, and computational perturbation to characterize β-cell identity-associated molecular features. IAPP emerged as the sole overlapping candidate from the integrated machine-learning and PPI analyses and was reduced in T2DM islets. Its expression was positively corr

documents.title: Automated Chest Diseases Classification Using Multimodal Deep Learning.
documents.abstract: Computer-Aided Diagnosis systems can support physicians by reducing workload, medical errors, and time required for patient care. However, many existing systems primarily rely on medical images while overlooking valuable information available in associated medical reports. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning approach for chest disease classification by integrating chest X-ray images and radiology reports from the MIMIC-CXR dataset. (2) Methods: Different Deep Learning models are evaluated for each modality, followed by a comprehensive comparison of intermediate and late fusion strat

documents.title: Fungal laccases: a double-edged sword linking environmental adaptation and pathogenicity.
documents.abstract: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2) are multicopper oxidases that oxidize diverse phenolic and non-phenolic compounds while reducing oxygen to water. Despite their highly conserved catalytic architectures, fungal laccases perform diverse biological functions depending on ecological context. In saprophytic fungi, they contribute to lignin degradation, nutrient acquisition, carbon cycling, and pollutant detoxification, supporting their application in bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biofuel production, and green chemistry. In certain pathogenic fungi, laccases contribute to lineage-specific processes as

documents.title: Reading the Host from the Virus: A Systematic Review of Sequence-Based Prediction of Host-Related Properties for Eukaryote-Infecting Viruses.
documents.abstract: Viral metagenomics and metatranscriptomics have expanded our understanding of viral diversity and associations between viruses and hosts. For eukaryotic viruses, identifying host-related properties remains challenging because infection depends on receptor compatibility, tissue specificity and mechanisms of immune evasion. Interspecies transmission and zoonotic spillover pose major risks to global health, highlighting the need for computational methods that can prioritise plausible host associations and related risks for known and novel viruses. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematical

documents.title: Integrating Inflammatory and Endothelial Biomarkers in Machine Learning Models to Predict Sepsis Development in Critically Ill Patients: A Combined Retrospective and Prospective Multicenter Study.
documents.abstract: Sepsis is a severe, life-threatening condition in which timely recognition improves patient outcomes. Machine learning (ML) methods, usually relying on vital sign data, have shown promise in early sepsis prediction; however, they underrepresent sepsis biomarkers, which are widely used in clinical practice. We aimed to develop and validate interpretable ML models for early sepsis prediction using non-temporal data from the first 24 h of intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and to quantify the incremental value of inflammatory (Interleukin-6 (IL-6), procalcitonin (PCT), C-Reactive Protein (CRP))

documents.title: Predicting Pediatric Appendicitis: A Comparative Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Routine Laboratory Parameters.
documents.abstract: Background: Routine laboratory blood tests are central in evaluating children with suspected appendicitis. Machine learning (ML) offers promise for improving diagnostic accuracies by predicting from variables that are non-linearly associated. We explored and internally validated ML models in their prediction of appendicitis with routine laboratory parameters in comparison with logistic regression and established clinical algorithms. Methods: We carried out a secondary analysis of a public dataset of 780 children admitted with suspected appendicitis of which 463 (59.4%) were diagnosed with appe

documents.title: Quercetin Alleviates PFOS-Induced Inflammatory Responses in Human Microvascular Endothelial Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) is a ubiquitous industrial chemical linked to cardiovascular toxicity. Quercetin, a plant-derived flavonoid, exhibits known anti-inflammatory properties. While PFOS induces endothelial dysfunctions, the molecular mechanisms underlying quercetin's protective effects remain unclear. Methods: We integrated transcriptomic analysis and in vitro experiments to investigate these mechanisms in human microvascular endothelial cells (HMEC-1). Results: Five overlapping hub genes between PFOS and quercetin targets (IL6, RELA, VEGFA, CXCL8 and PIM1) were ide

documents.title: Treatment Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Conceptual Framework for Precision Therapy.
documents.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a major therapeutic challenge, with limited improvement in outcomes and substantial heterogeneity in treatment response. Systemic chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of treatment across disease stages, yet treatment selection, particularly in metastatic PDAC (mPDAC), is still driven predominantly by clinical characteristics, performance status, prior therapy, and a limited number of molecular biomarkers. The emergence of biomarker-directed therapies, including strategies targeting oncogenic KRAS alterations, demonstrates the potential of molecular

documents.title: Combining Machine Learning Approaches and In Vitro Assays to Identify Novel ACE- and DPP-IV-Inhibitory Peptides from Complex Duckweed (Lemnoideae) Protein Hydrolysates.
documents.abstract: Identifying peptide sequences responsible for the bioactivity of complex food protein hydrolysates remains a challenge in the development of functional food ingredients, especially from novel protein sources such as duckweed (Lemnoideae) hydrolysates. A dataset comprising 407 peptides, their features as well as the ACE and DPP-IV inhibitory activities of the different global fractions was constructed, and four complementary statistical and machine learning approaches, Random Forest regression, Partial Least Squares regression, Linear Regression, and Pearson correlation, were applied to associa

documents.title: Cross-Disease Integration Identifies Inflammation-Related Candidate Biomarkers for Atherosclerosis and Candidate Therapeutic Compounds Using Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
documents.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a translational research framework integrating cross-disease computational screening with experimental validation. Using Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection as a cross-disease inflammatory comparator, we systematically identified atherosclerosis-associated hub genes through integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses, evaluated their potential diagnostic value in independent datasets, and validated their protein expression in a mouse model of atherosclerosis (AS). Methods: GEO gene-expression datasets were analyzed using differential e

documents.title: Proteomics Reveals Stress-Related Proteins in the Embryonic Axis of Chickpea Sprouts Grown Under Green and Red LED Light.
documents.abstract: Stress-related proteins are overexpressed in plants under adverse growth conditions, helping them to survive. The identification and quantification of these proteins are limited in non-model organisms. Furthermore, the high concentration of storage proteins commonly found in seeds increases the difficulty of studying them. Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) is one of the most consumed legumes worldwide. Nevertheless, the proteins implicated in stress response have not been explored sufficiently in this organism. Light-emitting diode (LED) light has been used to improve crop quality for a long time;

documents.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
documents.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: A Comparison of Convolutional, Transformer, and State-Space U-Shaped Pipelines for Neuronal Soma Instance Segmentation in Label-Free 3D Microscopy.
documents.abstract: Instance segmentation of neuronal somata in label-free three-dimensional (3D) microscopy is challenging because of low contrast, crowding, and species- and modality-dependent appearance. We compared seven U-shaped semantic-to-instance pipelines (3D U-Net, nnU-Net v2, SwinUNETR, 3D TransUNet, U-Mamba, Swin-UMamba-3D, and an exploratory MedMamba-UNet) on 240 public volumes of six rat, mouse, and human species-modality subsets, using the released partition. Models were trained for 25,000 steps with three seeds, post-processing was selected on source-domain validation volumes, and native-grid pred

documents.title: Digital Twin-Enabled Multi-Sensor Framework for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Machinery.
documents.abstract: This paper presents a multi-sensor framework for condition monitoring and intelligent fault diagnosis in rotating industrial machinery, integrating heterogeneous sensing, machine-learning-based diagnosis, MQTT communication, historical data management, and a synchronized 3D Digital Twin. The experimental platform employs feature-level fusion by combining statistical and spectral descriptors extracted from vibration and acoustic signals with temporally aligned temperature and rotational-speed measurements to classify four machine-health states: Healthy, Minor, Moderate, and Severe. To assess th

documents.title: Genomic Prediction for Powdery Mildew Resistance in Wheat: A Thirty-Model Benchmark of Conventional, Machine-Learning, and Deep-Learning Approaches.
documents.abstract: Powdery mildew, caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt), is a major foliar disease of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). Genomic prediction (GP) can accelerate breeding for this trait, but conventional, machine-learning (ML), and deep-learning (DL) methods have rarely been compared side by side. Using the Wheat Association Mapping Initiative (WAMI) panel (n = 286), phenotyped for powdery mildew severity over three years (DS1-DS3) and genotyped with the Illumina 90K SNP array, we compared 30 GP models under per-year and genotype-grouped pooled cross-validation. Broad-sense heritabilit

documents.title: Multi-Omics and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Reveal Peimine Modulates Macrophage Polarization Homeostasis via CCR3/ITK/S1PR5/PRKCQ and MMP8/UGCG/KLF5 Axes in Pneumonia.
documents.abstract: Pneumonia is driven by disordered immune inflammation dominated by dysregulated macrophage polarization. Peimine, the major bioactive steroidal alkaloid of Fritillariae Bulbus, exerts anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, whereas its direct targets and the metabolic routes through which it may influence macrophage polarization in pneumonia remain unclear.

documents.title: StrongGeneAgent: An Evidence-Grounded Conversational Agent for Gene-Centric Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis.
documents.abstract: Single-gene analysis remains a common entry point for investigating cancer biology, yet integrating evidence for a target gene across molecular layers, tumor types, and clinical endpoints remains fragmented across specialized tools and workflows. Here, we present StrongGeneAgent, an evidence-grounded conversational framework for natural-language, gene-centric multi-omics analysis across cancer types.

documents.title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis.
documents.abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. Inspired by this biological selective-attention mechanism, we propose a segmentation-guided framework in which a modality-aware 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) first delineates the prostate gland from T2-weighted, ADC, and

documents.title: Systemic Inflammatory Markers and Quantitative Stool Culture in Machine Learning Classification of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: An Exploratory Case-Control Study.
documents.abstract: Machine learning (ML) studies of the gut microbiota rarely test whether microbial data add anything to routine clinical and inflammatory markers. We examined this question in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) using quantitative stool culture. In this exploratory case-control study, 52 adults with IBD and 34 hospital controls underwent clinical, anthropometric, bioimpedance, biochemical and inflammatory assessment, together with quantitative stool culture interpreted against laboratory reference intervals. Six classifiers were evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation (5 folds × 10 repeats

documents.title: Explainable Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Differential Diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuromyelitis Optica Using 3D MRI Lesion Features.
documents.abstract: Neurological disorders are among the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide, making timely and accurate diagnosis essential. Differential diagnosis (DD) of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) and Neuromyelitis Optica (NMO) spectrum disorder using brain MRI remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and similar lesion characteristics. To address this challenge, this study proposes a neuroinformatics-driven computer-aided differential diagnosis (CADD) framework that automatically extracts, encodes, and analyzes quantitative 3D lesion biomarkers from brain MRI using deep lea

documents.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
documents.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Protify: A Benchmarking Platform Revealing Task Dependence and Homology Leakage in Protein Language Model Evaluation.
documents.abstract: Protein Language Models (pLMs) have become essential tools for computational protein analysis, and the rapid proliferation of architectures, training objectives, and pretraining corpora has produced a diverse and expanding model landscape. Evaluation practices, however, remain fragmented: studies use different datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and reporting conventions, so results rarely transfer between publications. Here we introduce Protify, an open-source platform that standardizes pLM benchmarking across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings through a unified, low-code in
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction.
documents.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ∼15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: CASP1 and SPTAN1 Identified as Potential PANoptosis-Related Biomarkers for Differentiating Active Tuberculosis from Latent Tuberculosis Infection Through Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis and Exploratory In Vitro Assessment.
documents.abstract: Distinguishing active tuberculosis (ATB) from latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) remains a critical unmet need in tuberculosis control. PANoptosis, a newly recognized form of programmed cell death (PCD) integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, may provide novel biomarkers for this distinction. To explore this, transcriptomic datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were employed to identify PANoptosis-related differentially expressed genes (TPAN_DEGs) between ATB and LTBI. An ensemble machine-learning approach combining least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), S

documents.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
documents.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Outcomes Reported in Randomised Controlled Trials of Pharmacological Treatments for Acute Viral Respiratory Infections in Hospitalised Adults: A Rapid Scoping Review.
documents.abstract: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of pharmacological treatments for acute viral respiratory infections (AVRIs) report outcomes that vary in selection, definition, timing, and measurement, thereby hampering evidence synthesis and comparability across clinical trials. This rapid scoping review mapped the outcomes, definitions, time points, and measurement instruments reported in RCTs of pharmacological treatments for hospitalised adults with AVRIs. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from June 2015 to June 2025 for RCTs, including adaptive and platform trials, that enroled hospitalised ad

documents.title: Physics-informed neural networks for estimation of volume and surface optical parameters in skin hyperspectral imaging using one- and two-layer tissue models.
documents.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a non-invasive optical modality capable of characterizing biological tissues, making it suitable for medical applications such as skin lesion analysis. However, recovering physiological and optical tissue parameters from hyperspectral skin data remains a challenging inverse problem due to the high dimensionality and complexity of light-tissue interactions. We hypothesize that physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can separate surface and volume reflections while recovering optical properties directly from hyperspectral skin images. To test this hypothesis, fou

documents.title: ADCCR: Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement for Language-Guided Human Keypoint Localization.
documents.abstract: Biological vision integrates cues according to their reliability and context and uses coarse contextual information to form initial hypotheses before directing attention to local evidence. Inspired by these principles, we propose ADCCR (Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement), a language-guided framework for flexible human keypoint localization. A multi-granularity bank describes each keypoint by its name, anatomical definition, inter-joint relation, and visual appearance. A reliability-aware composer predicts sample-specific gates from the person image, target identity

documents.title: Lineage-aware evaluation of machine learning for observed cross-genus occurrence of IncC plasmids in public databases.
documents.abstract: IncC plasmids contribute to the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance across bacterial hosts. We developed an IncC-specific model to classify plasmids belonging to highly similar cross-genus pairs observed in public databases and evaluated its performance when related lineages were kept together during validation.

documents.title: Cross-channel temporal fusion for retail customer lifetime value prediction: architecture, ablation, and causal validation of a gated BiGRU fusion network.
documents.abstract: Predicting customer lifetime value (CLV) in non-contractual retail settings is complicated by purchase sequence sparsity and heterogeneous engagement across marketing channels.

documents.title: Discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and hypertensive heart disease using deep learning-based magnetic resonance imaging.
documents.abstract: Discrimination between HCM and HHD can be challenging due to overlapping imaging presentation and clinical features. This study aimed to develop a deep learning pipeline for discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and hypertensive heart disease (HHD) using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images.

documents.title: Clinical effectiveness of Biqi capsule combined with methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis: an integrated retrospective, meta-analytic, and machine learning study.
documents.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) monotherapy provides inadequate disease control in many patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Biqi Capsule (BQC), a proprietary traditional Chinese medicine formulation, is used as an adjunct to MTX, but its clinical benefits remain uncertain.

documents.title: Anesthesia-associated pro-inflammatory microglial transcriptional signatures: transcriptomic identification and multi-dataset characterization of five candidate hub genes.
documents.abstract: To identify candidate hub genes associated with anesthesia-related microglial pro-inflammatory transcriptional changes and to explore their computationally inferred upstream transcriptional regulators, providing candidate molecular correlates that require future clinical validation before any relevance to perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) can be inferred.

documents.title: Selective representation learning boosts intrinsically disordered protein prediction from pretrained language models.
documents.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins and intrinsically disordered regions lack stable tertiary structures yet play indispensable roles in cellular signaling, regulation, and disease processes. Predicting disorder from sequence alone remains a fundamental challenge in computational biology. Recent advances in pretrained protein language models have shown great potential in capturing rich contextual representations. However, hierarchical pretrained protein language model features suffer from token-level noise and multi-layer redundancy, which limits their efficacy in downstream tasks.

documents.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
documents.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. documents.title: ToxiFusion: integrating contextual and compositional sequence representations for toxic peptide prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurately predicting of toxic peptides from sequence information is important for peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. However, reported performance of computational predictors can be affected by representation limitations and evaluation bias.
